effective.basis: TCG release of Yugi's Legendary Decks (YGLD-ENB22), the last dated printing before the current text

transitions.historical_text: Pay 1000 Life Points. Select 1 Level 7 or higher Spellcaster-Type monster you control. During this turn, only the selected monster can attack, and it must attack all monsters your opponent controls once each. The effects of monsters destroyed by battle with it are not activated.
transitions.modern_text: Pay 1000 LP, then target 1 Level 7 or higher Spellcaster-Type monster you control; this turn, only that monster can attack, and it must attack all monsters your opponent controls, once each. The effects of Effect Monsters destroyed by these attacks do not activate and are negated.
transitions.summary: Problem-Solving Card Text modernisation collapsing v3 (LCYW-EN066), v4 (DPYG-EN023 reprint) and v5 (YGLD-ENB22): 'Select' becomes 'target', 'Life Points' becomes 'LP', and 'The effects of monsters destroyed by battle with it are not activated' becomes 'The effects of Effect Monsters destroyed by these attacks do not activate and are negated'. Resolution is unchanged - the same single Level 7 or higher Spellcaster is compelled to attack every opposing monster once each while your other monsters cannot attack.

transitions.summary: Wording only, on period rulings (round 037, 2026-09-29). The record claimed: The modern card requires that the opponent controls a monster to activate; the claim is that the era card could be activated (paying 1000 LP and locking your other monsters out of attacking) while the opponent controlled no monsters. A period ruling in force says otherwise: Konami TCG Card FAQ default_de page (Internet Archive capture served 2008-12-15): "You cannot activate "Diffusion Wave-Motion" during Main Phase 2, or if you cannot conduct your Battle Phase this turn (if you activated "Soul Exchange", etc.), or if there are no monsters on your opponent's side of the field" No difference between the era card and the modern card is established.

review.notes:
Era text at the Edison snapshot (2010-04-24) is v2 (DPYG-EN023, 2009-07-07); the GOAT-era text is v1 (DR1-EN162, 2005-03-19) and differs from v2 only in wording ('must attack', 'your opponent controls'), so the recorded chain starts at v2 and v0 (MFC-107, 2003-10-10, which lacked 'once each') is left out of it. NO HISTORICAL IMPLEMENTATION IS RECORDED DESPITE THE FUNCTIONAL VERDICT: upstream's official/c87880531.lua gates activation on 'e1:SetCondition(s.condition)' where 's.condition' returns 'Duel.IsAbleToEnterBP()' only - it does not implement the printed 'If your opponent controls a monster:' requirement - so the shipped implementation already reproduces the era activation legality and nothing plays wrongly today. Flagged conflicting-evidence because upstream's script contradicts the card's own current printed text; if upstream ever implements that condition, this card needs a historical implementation and a reserved passcode. The packet's only upstream entry, 511600096 'Diffusion Wave-Motion (Manga)', implements the manga card (any Spellcaster, no Level restriction, no 'other monsters cannot attack' field effect) and is not a TCG-era implementation.

Round 037 (2026-09-29). Checked against period rulings: the differences the functional transition claims were searched for in the Konami-hosted UDE card FAQ (2008-12), the 2005 UDE card rulings page, Konami's errata lists, rulebooks and per-set ruling documents, and the archived UDE judge-list threads Yugipedia points to (the transition's rulings_check; docs/research/text-only-errata-audit.md, Diffusion Wave-Motion). A period ruling in force contradicts every difference the transition claimed: The modern card requires that the opponent controls a monster to activate; the claim is that the era card could be activated (paying 1000 LP and locking your other monsters out of attacking) while the opponent controlled no monsters. Contradicted by Konami TCG Card FAQ default_de page (Internet Archive capture served 2008-12-15): "You cannot activate "Diffusion Wave-Motion" during Main Phase 2, or if you cannot conduct your Battle Phase this turn (if you activated "Soul Exchange", etc.), or if there are no monsters on your opponent's side of the field" Upper Deck Entertainment official Yu-Gi-Oh! Card Rulings page (Internet Archive replay): "You cannot activate "Diffusion Wave-Motion" during Main Phase 2, or if you cannot conduct your Battle Phase this turn (if you activated "Soul Exchange", etc.), or if there are no monsters on your opponent's side of the field" The transition is cosmetic: no difference between the era card and the modern card is established. Verdicts: [c1] d1 contradicted at Edison, contradicted at Tengu. Variant-script points a ruling contradicts, listed for the owner (Ignis's script is not edited): Diffusion Wave-Motion: Ignis's script (the modern implementation the list uses) lets the card be activated against an empty field; the FAQ says it cannot be. An implementation gap, not a history question. Superseded summary, kept verbatim: "The current text gained an activation requirement the era card did not have: 'If your opponent controls a monster:'. Under the Edison-era printing (v2, DPYG-EN023) and every printing through v6 the card could be activated with the opponent controlling no monsters, paying 1000 LP and locking your other monsters out of attacking. The undated lineage entry v6 adds only the '(This card is not treated as a "Fusion" card.)' parenthetical and is folded into this transition." Superseded coverage, kept verbatim: kind: "none-needed".
